newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY GRAIN FUTURES END MIXED ON LAST '96 DAY.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY GRAIN FUTURES END MIXED ON LAST '96 DAY.

text.p: The last day of trade on Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) grain section ended without clear trends emerging for next year, traders said on Thursday.
"There is uncertainty about next year's export regulations although market talk has it that the new (agriculture) minister plans to liberalise exports," said Ferenc Kiss of Agrokont.
"Today's price changes do not show any trends," he added.
Maize futures closed unchanged at 19,600 forints for March 1997, at 19,700 for May, up 200 and at 19,900 forints for July, down 200.
In the last two weeks there was some Russian interest for Hungarian maize, but whether this can materialise in actual exports will depend on official regulations.
"Even if export is not allowed, prices are unlikely to drop further as they already are around production price levels (plus interest)," Kiss said.
Old (1996) crop milling wheat prices -- slightly above 28,000 forints -- are also around minimum levels, but could move in either direction depending again on export chances.
"Wheat prices are influenced by flour prices as Hungarian flour is easier to sell than wheat," Kiss said, adding that there is some demand for flour in neighbouring countries.
"Serbia is said to have oversold and would need to import," he added.
The long-term outlook for blackseed prices -- at a low of 43,030 to 43,900 forints -- is somewhat easier to predict, he said.
"In the last two to four years producers have planted larger areas than crop rotation would allow and they probably won't risk it again," Kiss said.
Blackseed pests can survive in the ground from one year to the next and consecutive years of planting thus considerably increase the chances of a bad crop, he said.
Total turnover of the BCE grain section on Thursday was 827.73 million forints, or 1,819 lots, of which 885 lots were maize and 764 milling wheat.
Total turnover for 1996 was 62.5 billion forints.
The next day of grain trading will be January 2.
(Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts. $1=164.67 forints)
